title: Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS), 14:00 ET
source: EST: derived from federalreserve.gov's own published 2027 FOMC calendar (monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200 — April 27-28, then June 8-9, no May meeting) plus a release-date rule AUDITED THIS SESSION against 67 SLOOS releases, 2010-02-01 through 2026-08-03. Release dates were read from each edition page's Last Update field on federalreserve.gov/data/sloos (and the legacy /boarddocs/SnLoanSurvey pages back to 1997), cross-validated 13 for 13 against the Fed's own newsevents monthly calendars for 2023-05 through 2026-08, which list SLOOS at 2:00 p.m. The rule that fits 64 of 67 is 'the Monday five sessions after the FOMC's final day'; all three exceptions are business-day shifts of that same Monday with a named cause -- 2012-10-31 (Hurricane Sandy shut the market Monday 10-29 and Tuesday 10-30), 2018-11-13 and 2024-11-12 (the Monday was Veterans Day, a federal holiday on which the NYSE trades but the Board is closed). 2027-05-03 is an ordinary Monday, so the refined rule and the naive one agree. Filed estimate on three counts: federalreserve.gov publishes no 2027 newsevents page (2027-may.htm and 2027-february.htm both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-09), so neither the date nor the 14:00 ET slot can be read from a primary; the FOMC calendar it derives from carries the Fed's own caveat that 'each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it'; and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03, 2026-09-09; canonical file written by its own initial research, 2026-09-09
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT -- and the refusal is now measured on n=67 rather than the sibling's n=3. KRE's close-to-close excess vs SPY across every modern-regime release (2010-02-01 -> 2026-08-03) is +0.109% on 32/67 up (permutation p=0.496), and -0.074% (p=0.649) once the two days above KRE's own p90 are removed -- both of which have named non-SLOOS causes (2020-11-09 was the Pfizer vaccine Monday, +14.17%; 2023-05-08 was the week after the First Republic seizure, -2.03%). KBE +0.162% (p=0.262) and XLF +0.085% (p=0.321) agree. THE ONE TRAP THIS SESSION FOUND: 63 of the 67 releases are Mondays, so an all-session control makes SLOOS days look like a volatility event -- VIX +2.973%, p=0.008 -- when all Mondays since 2010 average +1.878% (n=785) and Mondays that are NOT SLOOS days average +1.756%. Against the weekday-matched pool the effect is +3.268%, p=0.126: it is the Monday effect, not the survey. Any fixed-weekday event on this calendar must be tested against its own weekday's pool. 2027-05-03 is also the first trading day of May (2027-05-01 is a Saturday), and first-business-day Mondays run SPY +0.275% (p=0.042, n=77) on their own, which is the honest owner of the equity drift treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03 leg 7 attributes to that session; against that pool the SLOOS subset is +0.386%, p=0.317. What earns this edition a row is TIMING plus one content change. Timing: the survey's response window closes about 2027-04-02 (derived from 32 editions' published sent/due dates -- April editions go out the Monday after the March FOMC and are due 28-31 days before release), so it reads bank views formed right after the 2027-03-17 decision and is already about a month stale relative to the 2027-04-28 meeting whose Monday it follows. Content: the April-2026 and July-2026 editions both carried special questions on lending to NONDEPOSITORY FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS -- the bank credit that funds private credit -- which is the channel sloos-2026-11-02 explicitly ruled out for CRWV. Two consecutive editions is a series, not a one-off; whether it recurs on 2027-05-03 is a registered forward test. Its signal is buried by construction: ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03 (est, 10:00 ET) leads it by four hours and treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03 (est, 15:00 ET) follows it by one, the FOMC decided 04-28, refunding lands 05-05 and payrolls 05-07. Like the Beige Book it is Fed-funded and publishes through an appropriations lapse where BLS data does not. Nothing here licenses an entry; the date is an estimate and an estimate only widens caution.
